purpose: Inverse trajectory control in a quasi-2D gas-liquid bubble column: given a target particle path, solve for the gas-distributor zone configuration (static or dynamic switching sequence) that produces it. Main contribution is the inverse-problem framework + dynamic switching for non-monotonic paths. Target: Chemical Engineering Journal.

geometry.note: 2D (empty front/back); 60 x 120 cells at 5 mm; liquid to 0.45 m, 0.15 m headspace for the free surface. Block order = zone order, ix fastest within a block.

physics.note: Solver settings follow the v2306 twoPhaseEulerFoam RAS/bubbleColumn tutorial (SchillerNaumann + segregated drag, virtual mass, mixtureKEpsilon, no lift). Inlet: alpha.air = alpha_inlet, U.air = Ug / alpha_inlet.

zones.constraint: mean(Ug1,Ug2,Ug3) == Ug_total (equal zone widths, fixed total gas flow)

particle.note: Neutrally buoyant tracer (St << 1): advected by the liquid velocity, RK4 on time-interpolated U.water snapshots. Particles reflect at walls and the free surface.

targets.note: Target paths: x [m] where the tracer crosses each height y [m] on its first ascent

thresholds.note: DRAFT - calibrate after the first baseline run
